01-01.title: New Orleans Bourbon Street truck attack
01-01.description: On January 1, 2025, Shamsud-Din Jabbar drove a pickup truck into crowds celebrating New Year on Bourbon Street, then opened fire, killing 14 people and injuring dozens before being fatally shot by police. The FBI classified the attack as a terrorist act inspired by the Islamic State, to which Jabbar pledged allegiance in videos posted before the attack.

01-05.title: Tel Aviv Central Bus Station double suicide bombing
01-05.description: Two suicide bombers attacked near Tel Aviv's old central bus station on January 5, 2003, killing 23 people, including eight foreign nationals, and injuring more than 100. The al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigade claimed responsibility.

01-07.title: Charlie Hebdo shooting
01-07.description: Gunmen attacked Charlie Hebdo's Paris office on January 7, 2015, killing 12 people, including journalists and police officers. The Kouachi brothers were killed by police two days later. Separate linked attacks killed five more people, bringing the January 7-9 victim total to 17.
sources: Committee to Protect Journalists, attack report

01-07.title: Los Angeles wildfires (Palisades and Eaton fires)
01-07.description: The Palisades and Eaton fires began in Los Angeles County on January 7, 2025 local time and were contained on January 31. CAL FIRE records 31 civilian deaths and 16,264 destroyed structures across the two fires.

01-08.title: Tucson mass shooting targeting Rep. Gabrielle Giffords
01-08.description: A gunman attacked Representative Gabrielle Giffords's constituent event in Tucson, Arizona, on January 8, 2011, killing six people and injuring 13, including Giffords. Jared Lee Loughner pleaded guilty to federal charges and in November 2012 was sentenced to life imprisonment without release.

01-09.title: Chinagodrar military camp attack
01-09.description: Militants attacked Niger's military post at Chinagodrar near the Mali border on January 9, 2020. Reuters subsequently reported that at least 89 Nigerien soldiers were killed. French fighter jets were sent to help repel the attackers.

01-10.title: China winter storms (2008 Chinese snowstorms)
01-10.description: A series of snow, freezing-rain and severe-cold episodes affected southern and central China beginning January 10, 2008, disrupting electricity and transport. The Asian Disaster Reduction Center's subsequent summary records 129 deaths across 20 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities.

01-12.title: Haiti Earthquake
01-12.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck near Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on January 12, 2010, devastating the capital and surrounding areas. PAHO and UN accounts report an estimated 220,000 deaths and about 300,000 injuries.

01-13.title: El Salvador Earthquake
01-13.description: An earthquake struck off El Salvador on 13 January 2001 at 17:33 UTC. USGS strong-motion documentation gives magnitude Mw 7.6. Official impact figures cited in a subsequent technical report were 944 deaths and 5,565 injuries, with more than 100,000 houses destroyed. Landslides caused extensive loss of life, including in Santa Tecla.

01-15.title: DusitD2 complex attack
01-15.description: Al-Shabaab attacked the DusitD2 hotel and business complex in Nairobi on January 15, 2019. Twenty-one victims were killed. Kenyan authorities said all five attackers also died. The toll of 21 excludes the attackers.

01-15.title: Yeti Airlines Flight 691 crash
01-15.description: Yeti Airlines Flight 691, an ATR 72-500 flying from Kathmandu, crashed on approach to Pokhara on January 15, 2023, killing all 68 passengers and four crew. Nepal's final investigation identified inadvertent movement of both condition levers to the feathered position as the most probable cause, resulting in loss of thrust, an aerodynamic stall and ground impact.

01-16.title: Mustansiriya University bombing
01-16.description: Bombing attacks near Mustansiriya University in Baghdad on January 16, 2007, killed about 70 people, many of them students, according to UNAMI. Numerous others were injured.

01-17.title: Gul Plaza shopping mall fire
01-17.description: A fire broke out at the Gul Plaza shopping centre in Karachi on the night of 17 January 2026. Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority subsequently reported at least 80 deaths and dozens of injuries; an earlier inquiry report counted 79 deaths. The fire spread through the multistorey commercial building.

01-18.title: Nigeria fuel tanker explosion in Suleja
01-18.description: A fuel tanker accident and explosion at Dikko junction in Niger State on January 18, 2025 killed people gathered around spilled fuel. NEMA reported 98 deaths and 69 injuries in its January 28 update.

01-20.title: Kano bombings
01-20.description: Boko Haram carried out coordinated bombings and shootings in Kano on January 20, 2012. Authorities reported 185 deaths, including about 150 civilians, 29 police officers and three state-security officers. Targets included police, state-security and immigration facilities.

01-22.title: Monterey Park mass shooting
01-22.description: A gunman attacked Star Ballroom Dance Studio in Monterey Park late on January 21, 2023 local time, January 22 UTC, killing eleven people and wounding nine. The attack occurred during Lunar New Year celebrations. He subsequently entered another dance hall in Alhambra, where he was disarmed, and later died by suicide.

01-22.title: Antioch High School shooting
01-22.description: On January 22, 2025, 17-year-old Solomon Henderson shot and killed one student and wounded another in the Antioch High School cafeteria in Nashville, then died by suicide. Police reported ten shots within 17 seconds.

01-23.title: West Bandung landslide
01-23.location: West Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia
01-23.description: Heavy rain triggered a landslide in Pasirlangu village, West Bandung Regency, at about 02:30 local time on 24 January 2026 (23 January UTC), burying homes. By 10 February, West Java police had identified 80 victims. Identification of additional remains was continuing.

01-24.title: Domodedovo International Airport suicide bombing
01-24.description: A suicide bombing at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport on January 24, 2011, killed 37 people and injured more than 170. Insurgent leader Doku Umarov claimed responsibility. Three accomplices received life sentences in 2013.

01-25.title: Egyptian Revolution of 2011
01-25.description: Mass protests against the rule of President Hosni Mubarak began across Egypt on January 25, 2011, and continued for 18 days until Mubarak's resignation on February 11. Security forces used live ammunition, tear gas and beatings against demonstrators, primarily in Cairo's Tahrir Square and other cities. Egypt's official fact-finding commission reported that 846 people were killed and 6,467 injured during the uprising, which it determined involved unlawful police use of lethal force against protesters.

01-25.title: Brumadinho dam disaster
01-25.description: Vale's Corrego do Feijao tailings dam collapsed at Brumadinho, Brazil, on January 25, 2019, killing 270 people. Local authorities and victims' families commemorate 272 victims when two unborn children are included. Identification and recovery of victims continued for years after the collapse.

01-26.title: Gujarat (Bhuj) Earthquake
01-26.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Gujarat near Bhuj on 26 January 2001 at 03:16 UTC, India's Republic Day. USGS reports at least 20,000 fatalities, 166,836 injuries and nearly a million buildings damaged or destroyed.

01-27.title: Kabul ambulance bombing
01-27.description: On January 27, 2018, a Taliban attacker detonated explosives carried in an ambulance in central Kabul. Afghanistan's interior minister reported the next day that 103 people had been killed and 235 wounded.

01-29.title: Unity oilfield plane crash
01-29.description: On January 29, 2025, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by Eagle Air on behalf of Light Air Services crashed shortly after takeoff from the Unity oilfield airstrip in Unity State, South Sudan, while carrying oil workers to Juba; 20 of the 21 people on board were killed.

01-30.title: Peshawar mosque bombing
01-30.description: A suicide bombing inside the Police Lines mosque in Peshawar on January 30, 2023 killed 84 people in the revised police count, mostly police personnel. A TTP commander claimed responsibility, but the group's spokesman denied involvement. Pakistani investigators later attributed the attack to Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, a TTP faction.

01-30.title: Potomac River mid-air collision (American Airlines Flight 5342)
01-30.description: At about 01:48 UTC on January 30, 2025 (the evening of January 29 locally), PSA Airlines Flight 5342 and a US Army UH-60L helicopter collided near Reagan Washington National Airport and fell into the Potomac River. All 64 people on the airliner and three helicopter crew members died.

02-02.title: Central Chile Wildfires
02-02.location: Viña del Mar, Valparaíso Region, Chile
02-02.description: Wildfires beginning on February 2, 2024 devastated communities around Vina del Mar in Chile's Valparaiso Region. Prosecutors later confirmed 138 deaths, including later fatalities, superseding lower early totals. Thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed.

02-03.title: Kwara State attacks
02-03.description: Armed extremists attacked Woro and Nuku in Kaiama, Kwara State, on the evening of 3 February 2026. Local officials and the Red Cross reported at least 162 deaths, while the state government initially gave a lower count. Homes were burned and residents abducted. Reports differed over the attackers' affiliation, and no group immediately claimed responsibility.

02-05.title: Novye Aldi massacre
02-05.description: Russian OMON police conducted a house-to-house purge of the Novye Aldi suburb of Grozny, summarily executing at least 62 civilians. The European Court of Human Rights later ruled Russia responsible.

02-05.title: Meinong (Kaohsiung) earthquake
02-05.description: An earthquake centred near Meinong in southern Taiwan struck at 19:57 UTC on February 5, 2016, or early February 6 locally. It caused severe building collapses in Tainan. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration records 117 deaths.
sources: Taiwan Central Weather Administration, event record
National Center for Research on Earthquake Engineering, study

02-06.title: Islamabad mosque suicide bombing
02-06.description: An attacker opened fire at the gates of the Khadija Tul Kubra Shia mosque in Islamabad's Tarlai area during Friday prayers on 6 February 2026 before detonating explosives. The death toll subsequently rose to 36. More than 100 people were injured. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

02-08.title: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) mall shooting
02-08.description: On February 8-9, 2020, a Thai soldier killed 29 people in a rampage in Nakhon Ratchasima that included a military base and Terminal 21 shopping mall. He was killed by security forces after an overnight siege, bringing the total including the attacker to 30. It was Thailand's deadliest mass shooting at the time.

02-10.title: Tumbler Ridge school shooting
02-10.description: An 18-year-old former student killed eight people in Tumbler Ridge on 10 February 2026: her mother and 11-year-old brother at a home, and five students and a teacher at the secondary school. The perpetrator also died by suicide, bringing the total dead to nine. Twenty-seven people were reported injured.

02-13.title: Second El Salvador Earthquake
02-13.description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck the San Vicente region of El Salvador on 13 February 2001 at 14:22 UTC, one month after the January disaster. It killed 315 people and caused further destructive landslides and building collapses.

02-14.title: Sunjiawan coal mine explosion
02-14.description: A gas explosion at the Sunjiawan coal mine's Haizhou shaft in Fuxin, Liaoning, on February 14, 2005, killed 214 people and injured 30, according to the official investigation.
sources: China Ministry of Emergency Management investigation

02-14.title: Parkland School Shooting
02-14.description: On February 14, 2018, a gunman killed 17 people and wounded 17 others at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida.

02-14.title: Pulwama attack
02-14.description: A Jaish-e-Mohammed suicide bomber attacked a convoy of Indian paramilitary police in Pulwama on February 14, 2019, killing 40 security personnel. The attack was followed by Indian airstrikes at Balakot and an aerial confrontation between India and Pakistan.

02-15.title: Petropolis floods and mudslides
02-15.description: Extreme rainfall caused catastrophic flooding and landslides in Petropolis, Brazil, on February 15, 2022. More than 250 mm fell within hours. A later disaster study recorded 233 deaths, the highest toll for a disaster in the city's history.

02-17.title: Southern Leyte mudslide buries Guinsaugon village
02-17.description: A major landslide buried Guinsaugon village in Saint Bernard, Southern Leyte, on February 17, 2006, after prolonged heavy rain. Homes and an elementary school were buried. IFRC's subsequent report records 1,126 deaths.
sources: Center for Excellence in Disaster Management

02-18.title: Daegu subway fire
02-18.description: An arson attack aboard a train at Jungangno station in Daegu spread to a second train on February 18, 2003. The fire killed 192 people and injured more than 140. Combustible interiors, smoke and failures in the evacuation response contributed to the disaster.

02-18.title: Samjhauta Express bombing
02-18.description: Bombs and fire struck two coaches of the Samjhauta Express near Panipat shortly before midnight on February 18, 2007. Later court reporting records 68 people killed, most of them Pakistani nationals.

02-19.title: Iran Ilyushin Il-76 military plane crash
02-19.description: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards Ilyushin Il-76 flying from Zahedan to Kerman struck Mount Sirach during its approach in poor weather on February 19, 2003. All 275 occupants died. The Bureau of Aircraft Accidents Archives describes a premature descent below the minimum descent altitude in poor visibility.

02-19.title: Pasta de Conchos coal mine explosion
02-19.description: A disaster at the Pasta de Conchos coal mine in Coahuila on February 19, 2006, killed 65 miners. Only two bodies were recovered during the earlier recovery efforts, leaving families campaigning for the recovery of the remaining victims. Renewed recovery operations later located additional remains.

02-19.title: Hanau far-right shootings
02-19.description: On February 19, 2020, a racist attacker killed nine people of immigrant backgrounds at sites in Hanau, Germany. He also killed his mother and died by suicide. Ten victims were killed; the perpetrator's death is excluded from this count. Authorities treated the attack as far-right terrorism.

02-21.title: Kaduna religious riots
02-21.description: Christian-Muslim violence broke out in Kaduna on 21 February 2000 during a protest against proposed Sharia legislation. A state judicial commission reported at least 1,295 deaths in the February violence. Later violence in May is excluded from that count; people interviewed by Human Rights Watch believed the total across the 2000 riots was substantially higher.

02-21.title: The Station nightclub fire
02-21.location: West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States
02-21.description: Pyrotechnics ignited polyurethane foam during a concert at The Station nightclub in West Warwick late on February 20 local time, February 21 UTC. The rapidly spreading fire killed 100 people and injured more than 200.

02-21.title: Christchurch earthquake
02-21.description: An earthquake struck Christchurch and surrounding Canterbury at 12:51 p.m. local time on February 22, 2011 (23:51 UTC February 21), causing widespread building collapses and damage. New Zealand Police records 185 deaths. Thousands of people were injured.

02-22.title: Mozambique floods and Cyclone Eline
02-22.description: Cyclone Eline worsened severe flooding already affecting Mozambique in February 2000. The wider flood and cyclone emergency killed about 700 people and affected about two million; these are cumulative emergency totals, not deaths or displacement on the landfall date alone.

02-24.title: Bogoro massacre
02-24.location: Bogoro, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo
02-24.description: FNI and FRPI fighters attacked Bogoro in Ituri on February 24, 2003, killing at least 200 civilians. The International Criminal Court convicted Germain Katanga in connection with the attack in 2014; Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui was acquitted in 2012.

02-24.title: Russian invasion of Ukraine
02-24.description: Russia began its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022. By early January 2023, UN human rights monitors had verified at least 6,919 civilian deaths since the invasion, while warning the actual toll was higher. This is a dated cumulative civilian count and excludes military deaths; it is not a count of deaths on February 24.

02-25.title: Severnaya coal mine explosions, Vorkuta
02-25.description: Methane explosions at the Severnaya mine in Vorkuta on February 25, 2016 killed four miners and trapped 26 others, who were subsequently presumed dead. A third explosion on February 28 killed five rescuers and another miner, bringing the toll to 36.

02-26.title: SuperFerry 14 bombing
02-26.description: A bomb aboard SuperFerry 14 caused a fire near Manila Bay at about 00:50 on February 27, 2004, local time, February 26 UTC. The attack was attributed to Abu Sayyaf. The reported death toll of 116 includes missing passengers presumed dead.

02-27.title: Godhra train burning
02-27.description: A coach of the Sabarmati Express caught fire following an attack near Godhra station on 27 February 2002, killing 59 passengers, including Hindu pilgrims and activists returning from Ayodhya. The incident was followed by widespread anti-Muslim violence in Gujarat.

02-28.title: Tempe passenger train collision
02-28.description: A passenger train and a freight train collided head-on near Tempe, Greece, late on February 28, 2023, killing 57 people. A 2025 safety investigation identified human error, outdated infrastructure and systemic railway failures. The crash triggered widespread protests over railway safety.

03-01.title: Abiemnom massacre
03-01.description: Armed attackers raided Abiemnom in South Sudan's Ruweng Administrative Area on 1 March 2026. Local authorities reported 169 deaths, including 90 civilians. The UN mission said about 1,000 people sought shelter at its base. Accounts differed over the attackers' affiliation and the number injured.
sources: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

03-04.title: Peshawar mosque bombing
03-04.description: A suicide bomber attacked a Shia mosque in Peshawar's Qissa Khwani Bazaar area during Friday prayers on March 4, 2022. Reporting the next day put the death toll at 63 after injured victims died. Islamic State's regional affiliate claimed responsibility.

03-06.title: Karrada double bombing in Baghdad
03-06.description: Two explosions struck Baghdad's Karrada shopping district on March 6, 2008. The second occurred as people gathered to help victims of the first. Subsequent reporting put the death toll at 68.

03-07.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 Disappearance
03-07.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 lost contact with air traffic control at about 17:22 UTC on March 7, 2014, during its Kuala Lumpur-Beijing flight. It carried 227 passengers and 12 crew. Later satellite evidence led investigators to search the southern Indian Ocean; all 239 aboard are presumed dead.

03-07.title: Bahia Blanca flash floods
03-07.description: Flash flooding struck Bahia Blanca and surrounding areas on March 7, 2025, after 290 mm of rain in 12 hours. The confirmed death toll reached 18 after identification of the last missing child in May.

03-07.title: Syrian coastal massacres of Alawites
03-07.description: A Reuters investigation documented 1,479 Alawites killed at 40 sites during the March 7-9, 2025 massacres in Syria's coastal region. Its reporting linked attackers through a chain of command to figures serving alongside the country's new leadership; the count does not include all deaths in the wider fighting.

03-10.title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crash
03-10.description: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX 8 flying from Addis Ababa to Nairobi, crashed near Bishoftu on March 10, 2019, about six minutes after takeoff. All 157 people aboard died.

03-11.title: Madrid Train Bombings
03-11.description: Bombs exploded on Madrid commuter trains during the morning rush hour on March 11, 2004. Spanish government accounts distinguish 192 victims of the train attacks from a police officer killed in the related Leganes explosion on April 3. More than 1,800 people were injured in the train bombings.

03-11.title: Winnenden School Shooting
03-11.description: On March 11, 2009, 17-year-old former student Tim Kretschmer killed 15 people in a shooting spree beginning at his former school in Winnenden, Germany, and ending in nearby Wendlingen. He later died by suicide, bringing the total number of deaths to 16 including the attacker.

03-11.title: Jaffar Express hijacking
03-11.description: Baloch Liberation Army militants hijacked the Jaffar Express in Balochistan on March 11, 2025. Pakistan's military reported 31 victims killed, 354 hostages rescued and 33 attackers killed when the operation ended the following day.

03-15.title: Christchurch Mosque Shootings
03-15.description: A gunman attacked the Al Noor Mosque and Linwood Islamic Centre in Christchurch, New Zealand, on March 15, 2019, killing 51 people.

03-16.title: Atlanta spa shootings
03-16.description: A gunman attacked three Atlanta-area massage businesses on March 16, 2021, killing eight people, including six women of Asian descent.

03-16.title: Kocani nightclub fire
03-16.description: A fire at the Pulse nightclub in Kocani on March 16, 2025 killed 63 people and injured more than 200, according to figures cited in court indictments. Investigators reported that pyrotechnics ignited flammable ceiling foam in a venue lacking adequate fire safety provisions.

03-19.title: Ulyanovskaya mine disaster
03-19.description: A methane explosion at the Ulyanovskaya coal mine near Novokuznetsk on March 19, 2007, killed 110 of the 203 people underground. Ninety-three survived, according to IFRC.

03-20.title: Chattisinghpora massacre
03-20.location: Chattisinghpora, Anantnag district, Jammu and Kashmir, India
03-20.description: Gunmen rounded up Sikh residents in Chattisinghpora in Anantnag district on March 20, 2000 and shot them, killing 35 people.

03-20.title: US-led invasion of Iraq
03-20.description: The US-led invasion of Iraq began on March 20, 2003, and Baghdad fell on April 9. Iraq Body Count's 2005 dossier recorded 7,299 civilian deaths during the invasion period through April 30. This is a documented period total, not deaths on the opening day or a comprehensive estimate of all war mortality.

03-21.title: Red Lake High School shooting
03-21.description: On March 21, 2005, a 16-year-old killed his grandfather and his grandfather's companion before attacking Red Lake High School. He killed a security guard, a teacher and five students there, then died by suicide. Ten people died in total, including the attacker.

03-21.title: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735 crash
03-21.description: China Eastern Airlines Flight MU5735, a Boeing 737-800 travelling from Kunming to Guangzhou, descended rapidly and crashed near Wuzhou, Guangxi, on March 21, 2022. All 132 people aboard died. The April 2022 preliminary investigation did not determine the cause; debris examination and flight-data analysis were continuing.

03-21.title: South Korea wildfire outbreak
03-21.description: Wildfires began in southeastern South Korea on March 21, 2025 and spread across several areas, including Uiseong and Sancheong. World Weather Attribution's April 30 account reported 32 deaths in the March outbreak; Copernicus also reports 32 deaths and around 5,000 buildings destroyed.

03-22.title: Oso Mudslide
03-22.description: A landslide near Oso, Washington, swept across the Stillaguamish River valley on March 22, 2014, destroying homes and killing 43 people. The final victim's remains were recovered that July.

03-22.title: Brussels airport and metro bombings
03-22.description: Suicide bombings struck Brussels Airport and Maalbeek metro station on March 22, 2016. Thirty-two victims died in the attacks. In 2023, the court recognized three later deaths as attributable to the attacks, bringing the official victim toll to 35.

03-22.title: Boulder supermarket shooting
03-22.description: A gunman killed ten people, including police officer Eric Talley, at the King Soopers supermarket in Boulder, Colorado, on March 22, 2021. Police captured the suspect alive. An arrest affidavit said he purchased a Ruger AR-556 semiautomatic pistol on March 16, six days before the attack.

03-22.title: Crocus City Hall Concert Hall Attack
03-22.description: Gunmen attacked Crocus City Hall in Krasnogorsk, outside Moscow, on March 22, 2024, shooting concertgoers and setting the venue on fire. AP's August 2025 trial reporting gives 149 deaths and more than 600 wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack.

03-23.title: Ogossagou massacre
03-23.description: Armed men attacked the Fulani part of Ogossagou village in central Mali at about 05:00 on March 23, 2019. A UN investigation concluded that at least 157 people were killed. It identified most attackers as traditional hunters, accompanied by men in military and civilian clothing.

03-25.title: Nahrin earthquake
03-25.description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck the Nahrin area of Baghlan Province on 25 March 2002. Later IFRC operational reporting estimated 800 deaths and 10,000 people left homeless. Early casualty estimates were substantially higher; this figure follows the later IFRC assessment.
sources: International Charter Space and Major Disasters

03-25.title: Capitol Hill massacre in Seattle
03-25.description: Kyle Huff killed six people and wounded two at a house party in Seattle's Capitol Hill neighborhood on March 25, 2006. He then died by suicide when confronted by police, bringing the total number of deaths to seven, including the attacker.

03-25.title: Kemerovo shopping mall fire
03-25.description: A fire at the Winter Cherry shopping and entertainment complex in Kemerovo, Russia, on March 25, 2018 killed 60 people, including children. Later investigations found serious fire-safety failures.

03-26.title: ROKS Cheonan sinking
03-26.location: Baengnyeong Island, Yellow Sea, South Korea
03-26.description: The South Korean corvette ROKS Cheonan sank near Baengnyeong Island on March 26, 2010, killing 46 of its 104 crew. A multinational investigation attributed the sinking to a North Korean torpedo. North Korea denied responsibility.
sources: United Nations, North Korean press conference

03-27.title: Park Hotel Passover massacre
03-27.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked the Park Hotel in Netanya during a Passover meal on 27 March 2002, killing 30 civilians and injuring more than 100. The attack was one of the triggers for Israel's Operation Defensive Shield.

03-27.title: Tal Afar truck bombings
03-27.description: Truck bombs struck markets in Tal Afar on March 27, 2007, collapsing buildings. Iraq Body Count records 152 deaths; a US Army history reports nearly 350 wounded. Subsequent reprisal killings are not included in this bombing toll.
sources: US Army Iraq War history volume2

03-29.title: Moscow Metro suicide bombings
03-29.description: Two female suicide bombers attacked the Moscow Metro on the morning of March 29, 2010. The reported death toll rose to 40. North Caucasus insurgent leader Doku Umarov claimed responsibility.

04-01.title: Solomon Islands earthquake and tsunami
04-01.location: Western and Choiseul provinces, Solomon Islands
04-01.description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck near Gizo at 20:39 UTC on April 1, 2007, the morning of April 2 locally, generating a destructive tsunami. The earthquake and tsunami killed 52 people in the Solomon Islands. The national disaster office's subsequent reconciliation reported no people still missing.

04-01.title: Mocoa mudslide, Colombia
04-01.description: Floodwater and debris swept through Mocoa in Colombia's Putumayo department on the night of March 31-April 1, 2017, April 1 UTC. The municipality's risk assessment records 336 deaths and more than 400 injuries.
sources: Colombia National Disaster Risk Management Unit

04-02.title: Garissa University College attack
04-02.description: Al-Shabaab gunmen attacked Garissa University College at dawn on April 2, 2015, shooting students and taking hostages. Kenya's interior minister subsequently reported 148 people killed, most of them students. Security forces ended the siege that day.

04-03.title: Binghamton Immigration Center Shooting
04-03.description: On April 3, 2009, a gunman attacked the American Civic Association in Binghamton, New York, killing 13 people and wounding four. The attacker then died by suicide, bringing the total deaths including him to 14.

04-04.title: First Battle of Fallujah
04-04.description: US forces began an assault on Fallujah on the night of April 4, 2004, after four American contractors were killed. Iraq Body Count cites about 800 reported Iraqi deaths across the April siege and estimates that 572-616 were civilians. These cumulative figures are estimates, not a single-day count.

04-04.title: Thane building collapse
04-04.description: A residential building under construction in Mumbra, Thane, collapsed on the evening of April 4, 2013. The final rescue-operation toll was 74 dead, including 23 women and 18 children. Dozens of people were injured.

04-05.title: Upper Big Branch Mine explosion
04-05.description: An explosion at Massey Energy's Upper Big Branch Mine near Montcoal, West Virginia, on April 5, 2010, killed 29 miners and injured two. MSHA identified systematic safety failures, including inadequate control of methane and coal dust, and concluded the disaster was preventable. It was the deadliest US coal mining disaster in 40 years.
sources: Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission

04-06.title: L'Aquila Earthquake
04-06.description: An earthquake struck Abruzzo and the city of L'Aquila at 3:32 a.m. local time on April 6, 2009. Italian Civil Protection records 309 deaths and more than 1,500 injuries. About 65,000 people were displaced.

04-07.title: Douma chemical weapons attack
04-07.description: On April 7, 2018, a chemical attack in Douma, Syria, killed 43 named people. In January 2023, the OPCW investigation team found reasonable grounds to believe that Syrian air forces dropped two cylinders containing chlorine on residential buildings, affecting dozens more people.

04-09.title: Palm Sunday church bombings, Egypt
04-09.description: Suicide bombings struck Coptic churches in Tanta and Alexandria on Palm Sunday, April 9, 2017. Islamic State claimed responsibility. The victim toll subsequently reached 47.

04-13.title: Yushu earthquake
04-13.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Yushu area of Qinghai, China, on April 13, 2010 UTC (April 14 locally). USGS records at least 2,698 deaths, 270 people missing and 12,135 injured, with extensive building damage.

04-14.title: Kumamoto earthquakes
04-14.description: A sequence of earthquakes struck Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan, beginning on April 14, 2016. The larger shock occurred at 16:25 UTC on April 15, April 16 locally. The prefecture records 50 direct deaths and 225 disaster-related deaths; the numeric toll here counts direct deaths only.

04-15.title: Air China Flight 129 crash
04-15.description: Air China Flight 129, a Boeing 767 flying from Beijing to Busan, struck Mount Dotdae during a circling approach to Gimhae Airport on 15 April 2002. Of 166 people aboard, 129 died and 37 survived.

04-15.title: Boston Marathon Bombing
04-15.description: On April 15, 2013, two bombs exploded near the Boston Marathon finish line, killing three people and injuring hundreds. The FBI identified the attackers as Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev; a subsequent manhunt ended with one dead and the other captured.

04-15.title: Sewol Ferry Sinking
04-15.description: The ferry Sewol began capsizing near Jindo, South Korea, at about 23:48 UTC on April 15, 2014, or the morning of April 16 locally. Of 476 people aboard, 304 died or remained missing and presumed dead, while 172 survived.

04-15.title: Sudan civil war begins
04-15.description: War between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces began on April 15, 2023. In its update covering events through November 24, ACLED recorded more than 12,190 reported political-violence deaths since the outbreak. This is a dated, incomplete reported-death count excluding indirect mortality, not a final toll of the war.

04-16.title: Virginia Tech shooting
04-16.description: On April 16, 2007, a student gunman killed 32 people and wounded 17 by gunfire in two attacks at Virginia Tech in Blacksburg, Virginia. Other people suffered injuries while escaping. The attacker died by suicide and is excluded from the 32 victims.
sources: Virginia Tech Review Panel via US DOJ

04-16.title: Ecuador earthquake (M7.8)
04-16.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck coastal Ecuador at 23:58 UTC on April 16, 2016, severely affecting the Pedernales area of Manabi Province. Ecuador's later national planning account reports 676 deaths and more than 16,600 injuries from the disaster.
sources: Ecuador national planning authority, Zone 4 agenda

04-17.title: Nigeria post-election violence
04-17.description: Violence erupted in northern Nigeria on April 17, 2011, as presidential-election results indicated Goodluck Jonathan had defeated Muhammadu Buhari. Human Rights Watch reported more than 800 deaths and over 65,000 displaced people in three days of election-related and communal attacks across 12 northern states, including unlawful killings by security forces.

04-18.title: al-Sadriya market bombing
04-18.description: A car bomb exploded at Baghdad's Sadriya food market on the afternoon of April 18, 2007. Iraq Body Count records 140 deaths in this attack, excluding other bombings across Baghdad that day.

04-20.title: Lushan earthquake
04-20.description: An earthquake struck Lushan County in Ya'an, Sichuan, at 00:02 UTC on April 20, 2013. Chinese authorities measured it at magnitude 7.0. Xinhua's later retrospective records 196 deaths.

04-21.title: Deepwater Horizon explosion and oil spill
04-21.description: The Deepwater Horizon drilling rig exploded in the Gulf of Mexico on the evening of April 20, 2010 local time (April 21 UTC), killing 11 workers. The damaged Macondo well released oil for 87 days. NOAA reports approximately 3.2 million barrels entered the Gulf, damaging marine and coastal ecosystems.

04-22.title: Ryongchon train explosion
04-22.description: An ammonium-nitrate explosion at Ryongchon railway station on April 22, 2004, devastated the surrounding town. IFRC reported 161 deaths and about 1,300 injuries. The French government's accident archive records 76 children among those killed.

04-24.title: Rana Plaza factory collapse
04-24.description: The eight-storey Rana Plaza building in Savar, Bangladesh, collapsed on the morning of April 24, 2013. The ILO's retrospective records 1,134 deaths; more than 2,500 people were injured. Cracks had appeared before the collapse, which intensified international efforts to improve garment-industry safety.
sources: ILO Vision Zero Fund, Rana Plaza

04-25.title: Amagasaki train derailment
04-25.description: A JR West commuter train derailed and struck an apartment building in Amagasaki on April 25, 2005. It entered a 70 km/h curve at about 116 km/h. The crash killed 107 people, including the driver, and injured 562.

05-02.title: Bojaya massacre
05-02.description: On 2 May 2002, during fighting between FARC guerrillas and paramilitaries in Bellavista, Bojaya, a cylinder bomb launched by FARC struck the church where civilians had taken shelter. Colombia's victims authority later recorded at least 79 deaths and more than 100 injuries; earlier reports had put the toll at 119.

05-02.title: Cyclone Nargis strikes Myanmar
05-02.description: Cyclone Nargis struck Myanmar on May 2-3, 2008, devastating the Ayeyarwady Delta and other areas. The joint government, ASEAN and UN assessment reported 84,537 deaths and 53,836 people missing as of June 24. The recorded toll includes reported deaths only, excluding the missing. About 2.4 million people were severely affected.

05-04.title: Mexico City metro overpass collapse
05-04.description: An elevated section of Mexico City Metro Line 12 collapsed beneath a train between Olivos and Tezonco late on May 3, 2021 local time, May 4 UTC. Twenty-six people died and 79 were injured.

05-04.title: South Kivu floods and landslides
05-04.description: Heavy rain on May 4, 2023 triggered flooding and mudslides in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, destroying parts of Bushushu and Nyamukubi. A later MONUSCO appeal reported an official toll of 438 dead and more than 5,000 missing. The missing-person estimate is separate from confirmed deaths.

05-06.title: Allen outlet mall shooting
05-06.description: A gunman killed eight people and wounded seven at Allen Premium Outlets in Allen, Texas, on May 6, 2023. A police officer who was at the mall on another call shot and killed the attacker. The eight-victim total excludes the gunman.

05-12.title: Wenchuan earthquake (Sichuan earthquake)
05-12.description: The Wenchuan earthquake struck Sichuan on May 12, 2008, at 14:28 local time, damaging towns and infrastructure across the region. Later official figures cited in engineering research were 69,227 deaths, 17,923 missing and 374,643 injured. The recorded toll includes reported deaths only, excluding the missing.
sources: Earthquake Engineering Field Investigation Team study

05-12.title: Kabul maternity hospital attack
05-12.description: Gunmen attacked the MSF-supported maternity wing of Dasht-e-Barchi hospital in Kabul on May 12, 2020. Afghan authorities reported 24 people killed and more than 20 injured. MSF subsequently confirmed that the dead included 16 mothers, one MSF midwife and two children aged seven and eight.

05-13.title: Enschede fireworks disaster
05-13.description: A fire at a fireworks depot escalated into massive explosions, killing 23 people including four firefighters. The blasts destroyed around 400 homes.

05-13.title: Jaipur bombings
05-13.description: A series of bombs exploded in Jaipur's old city on the evening of May 13, 2008. Later court reporting records 71 deaths and 185 injuries. Four men convicted in the serial-blast case were acquitted by the High Court in 2023; four men were convicted in a separate related unexploded-bomb case in 2025.

05-13.title: Soma Coal Mine Disaster
05-13.description: A fire in the Eynez coal mine at Soma, Turkey, on May 13, 2014, killed 301 miners. Toxic gases, including carbon monoxide, were central to the deaths. Later investigations examined the fire's origin and serious mine-safety failures.

05-14.title: Gaza border protest killings
05-14.description: Israeli forces killed 60 Palestinians during demonstrations near the Gaza perimeter fence on May 14, 2018. A subsequent UN inquiry reported more than 1,100 people shot that day. Across demonstrations from March 30 through December 31, 2018, the inquiry recorded 189 Palestinian deaths, including 183 caused by live ammunition.

05-14.title: Buffalo supermarket shooting
05-14.description: A white supremacist gunman attacked a Tops supermarket in Buffalo, New York, on May 14, 2022, killing ten Black people and injuring three others. He later pleaded guilty to state charges and received life imprisonment without parole.

05-16.title: Casablanca bombings
05-16.description: Coordinated suicide bombings struck several sites in Casablanca on May 16, 2003, including a Spanish restaurant and Jewish-associated targets. The reported total of 45 deaths includes 33 victims and 12 bombers; about 100 people were injured.

05-18.title: Cubana de Aviación Flight 972 crash
05-18.description: On May 18, 2018, a Boeing 737 operating for Cubana de Aviacion crashed into a field shortly after departing Havana's Jose Marti International Airport. Of the 113 people aboard, 112 died and one survived. The aircraft was operated by Mexican charter company Global Air.

05-22.title: Air India Express Flight 812 crash
05-22.description: On May 22, 2010, Air India Express Flight 812, a Boeing 737-800 arriving from Dubai, overran the runway at Mangalore and crashed down an embankment. Of 166 people aboard, 158 died. The investigation found that the aircraft touched down far beyond the normal touchdown area after an unstabilized approach and that the captain failed to discontinue the landing.

05-22.title: Joplin tornado
05-22.description: An EF5 tornado struck Joplin, Missouri, on May 22, 2011, causing 158 direct deaths and more than 1,000 injuries, according to the National Weather Service. Its path extended about 22 miles.

05-22.title: Manchester Arena bombing
05-22.description: Salman Abedi detonated a suicide bomb at Manchester Arena as an Ariana Grande concert ended on May 22, 2017. Twenty-two victims were killed, excluding the bomber. His brother Hashem was later convicted of helping plan and prepare the attack.
sources: Greater Manchester Police, Hashem Abedi conviction

05-22.title: Qinyuan coal mine explosion
05-22.description: On 22 May 2026, an explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Qinyuan County, Shanxi Province, China, killed at least 82 miners, the worst coal-mining blast in China in more than a decade. The blast in one of China's major coal-producing regions prompted a state investigation into safety practices.

05-24.title: Uvalde School Shooting
05-24.description: A gunman killed 19 children and two teachers at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, on May 24, 2022. A US Justice Department review found a 77-minute gap between officers first arriving and confronting and killing the attacker. The victim count excludes the attacker.

05-25.title: China Airlines Flight 611 disaster
05-25.description: China Airlines Flight 611, a Boeing 747 traveling from Taipei to Hong Kong, broke up in mid-air about 20 minutes after takeoff and crashed into the Taiwan Strait. All 225 passengers and crew were killed.

05-25.title: Houla massacre
05-25.description: At least 108 people were killed in the Houla area of Syria on May 25, 2012. Human Rights Watch reported survivor accounts of executions following shelling and called for an independent investigation.

05-26.title: Yogyakarta earthquake
05-26.description: An earthquake struck the Yogyakarta and Central Java regions at about 05:54 on May 27, 2006, local time, May 26 UTC. Bantul and Klaten suffered severe damage. A subsequent IFRC report cites an official toll of 5,749 deaths and more than 38,000 injuries.

06-01.title: Dolphinarium Discotheque Bombing
06-01.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked outside the Dolphinarium discotheque in Tel Aviv on June 1, 2001, killing 21 other people, most of them teenagers, and injuring at least 120.

06-01.title: Nepalese Royal Palace Massacre
06-01.description: A shooting at Narayanhity Royal Palace in Kathmandu on 1 June 2001 ultimately left ten members of Nepal's royal family dead, including King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and Crown Prince Dipendra. An official inquiry attributed the killings of nine relatives to Dipendra, who died on 4 June. Gyanendra succeeded him as king.

06-02.title: Odisha train collision
06-02.description: On June 2, 2023, the Coromandel Express collided with a stationary freight train near Bahanaga Bazar in Odisha, and derailed coaches struck another passenger train. India's Ministry of Railways later reported 296 deaths. The disaster prompted investigations into signaling and railway safety failures.

06-05.title: Solhan village massacre
06-05.description: Armed attackers struck Solhan in Burkina Faso early on June 5, 2021, killing civilians including children and forcing residents to flee. Contemporary reporting put the provisional toll at about 160; UNICEF reported more than 130 civilian deaths. The larger number is a reported estimate, not a reconciled final count.

06-12.title: Orlando Pulse nightclub shooting
06-12.description: A gunman attacked Pulse nightclub in Orlando in the early hours of June 12, 2016, killing 49 victims. The shooting became a hostage incident before police killed the attacker later that morning.

06-12.title: Air India Flight 171 crash
06-12.description: Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 bound for London Gatwick, crashed shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad at about 08:09 UTC on June 12, 2025, striking B. J. Medical College hostel buildings. The official preliminary report records 241 deaths among 242 people aboard and 19 deaths on the ground.
sources: Ministry of Civil Aviation parliamentary answer

06-13.title: Grenfell Tower fire
06-13.description: A fire in a fourth-floor flat at Grenfell Tower in London spread through the building's combustible exterior cladding, killing 72 people. It was reported shortly before midnight UTC on June 13, 2017, June 14 locally.

06-14.title: Hajj Extreme Heat Deaths
06-14.description: During the June 14-19, 2024 Hajj pilgrimage, extreme heat caused mass mortality among pilgrims in Saudi Arabia. WHO reported Saudi authorities' total of 1,301 deaths from heat exhaustion, with 83% among unauthorized pilgrims walking long distances. The toll covers the pilgrimage period, not a single day.
sources: Saudi Ministry of Municipalities and Housing

06-14.title: Shooting of Minnesota state legislators
06-14.location: Brooklyn Park and Champlin, Minnesota, United States
06-14.description: On June 14, 2025, Vance Boelter killed Minnesota Representative Melissa Hortman and her husband Mark at their Brooklyn Park home and wounded Senator John Hoffman and his wife Yvette in Champlin. After his arrest, he pleaded guilty to federal murder and related charges on June 11, 2026; the separate state prosecution remained pending as of September 21, 2026.

06-16.title: Mpondwe school massacre
06-16.description: An attack blamed on Allied Democratic Forces rebels at Mpondwe-Lhubiriha Secondary School in western Uganda on June 16, 2023 killed 42 people, according to a June 19 official update, including 37 students. Attackers set a dormitory on fire; victims also suffered gunshot and machete attacks.

06-18.title: Jerusalem bus 32A bombing
06-18.description: A Hamas suicide bomber attacked Egged bus 32A near Patt Junction in Jerusalem during the morning rush hour on 18 June 2002, killing 19 other people and wounding more than 70.

06-18.title: Charleston church shooting
06-18.description: Dylann Roof killed nine Black worshippers during a Bible study at Emanuel AME Church in Charleston on the evening of June 17, 2015, local time, or June 18 UTC. He was arrested the next day and later convicted on federal hate-crime charges and sentenced to death.

06-21.title: Afghanistan earthquake (Khost and Paktika)
06-21.description: An earthquake struck Khost and Paktika in southeastern Afghanistan at 20:54 UTC on June 21, 2022, early June 22 locally. USGS lists magnitude 6.0. The UN's 2022 results report estimated 1,036 deaths, 2,924 injuries and damage to at least 4,500 homes.

06-22.title: Bou'in-Zahra earthquake
06-22.description: An earthquake struck the Avaj and Changureh area of northwestern Iran on June 22, 2002 at 02:58 UTC, severely damaging villages in Qazvin and neighboring regions. A disaster-science field report recorded about 261 deaths.
sources: Japan Society for Natural Disaster Science

06-24.title: Surfside condominium collapse
06-24.description: The 12-storey Champlain Towers South condominium in Surfside, Florida, partially collapsed at about 01:30 local time on June 24, 2021, killing 98 people. NIST opened a technical investigation into the collapse.

06-24.title: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
06-24.description: Two earthquakes, reported at magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela on 24 June 2026, causing widespread destruction, particularly in La Guaira. Official figures cited by UNICEF recorded 6,125 deaths as of 3 August. Homes and infrastructure were damaged and many residents displaced.

06-28.title: Atatürk Airport attack
06-28.description: Three suicide attackers struck Istanbul's Ataturk Airport on June 28, 2016. Forty-five victims were killed, excluding the three attackers.

07-01.title: Uberlingen mid-air collision
07-01.description: A Bashkirian Airlines Tupolev Tu-154 carrying 69 people, including many children en route to a Spanish holiday, collided with a DHL cargo Boeing 757 over southern Germany. All 71 people on both aircraft died.
sources: German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation

07-01.title: Irapuato rehabilitation center massacre
07-01.description: Three armed men attacked the Recuperando mi Vida rehabilitation centre in Irapuato, Guanajuato, on July 1, 2020. Later reporting put the death toll at 28. The killings occurred amid a series of attacks on rehabilitation centres in the state.

07-04.title: Typhoon Utor (Feria)
07-04.description: Utor, known as Feria in the Philippines, passed northern Luzon on 4 July 2001 and caused destructive flooding and landslides. A subsequent monthly storm summary reported at least 168 deaths in the Philippines. The storm then struck southern China, where additional deaths occurred; those are not included in this Philippine toll.

07-04.title: Highland Park parade shooting
07-04.description: A gunman opened fire from a rooftop during the Independence Day parade in Highland Park, Illinois, on July 4, 2022, killing seven people and injuring dozens. Prosecutors subsequently brought 117 charges, including 21 first-degree murder counts covering the seven victims.

07-06.title: Krasnodar Krai flash floods
07-06.description: Heavy overnight rain caused deadly flooding in Russia's Krasnodar region on July 6-7, 2012. A flood wave reached Krymsk early on July 7 local time, or July 6 UTC. The regional death toll was 171.

07-07.title: London bombings (7/7)
07-07.description: Four suicide bombers attacked three London Underground trains and a bus on July 7, 2005. The attacks killed 52 people, excluding the bombers, and injured more than 770.

07-08.title: Sudan Airways Flight 139 crash
07-08.description: Sudan Airways Flight 139, a Boeing 737, crashed near Port Sudan on July 8, 2003, killing 116 of its 117 occupants. After an engine failed following takeoff, the crew returned toward the airport; the aircraft struck terrain on approach in limited visibility.

07-08.title: Dallas police ambush
07-08.description: A gunman attacked police during a protest in Dallas on the evening of July 7, 2016, July 8 UTC. Five officers were killed and nine officers were wounded.

07-10.title: Victory declared in Mosul
07-10.description: Iraq declared victory over Islamic State in Mosul on July 10, 2017, while some fighting continued. An Associated Press investigation estimated 9,000-11,000 civilian deaths in the campaign from October 2016 to July 2017. The numeric toll is an approximate midpoint of that estimate.
sources: PBS interview with Associated Press investigator

07-12.title: 2006 Lebanon War
07-12.description: The war between Israel and Hezbollah lasted from July 12 to August 14, 2006. Human Rights Watch reported at least 1,109 deaths in Lebanon, mostly civilians, and about one million displaced people. The recorded toll is for Lebanon only; Israeli deaths are not included.

07-13.title: Mastung election rally bombing
07-13.description: A suicide bomber attacked a Balochistan Awami Party election rally near Mastung, Pakistan, on July 13, 2018. A subsequent official tally reported by Reuters put the deaths at 149, including candidate Siraj Raisani. Islamic State claimed responsibility.

07-14.title: Tropical Storm Bilis floods and landslides in China
07-14.description: Severe Tropical Storm Bilis made landfall on mainland China on July 14, 2006. Its prolonged rainfall caused extensive flooding and landslides across southern China. A meteorological study citing the China Meteorological Administration reports at least 843 deaths.

07-14.title: Nice Bastille Day truck attack
07-14.description: A truck was driven into crowds celebrating Bastille Day on Nice's Promenade des Anglais on July 14, 2016. Eighty-six people were killed and hundreds were injured. Police killed the driver.

07-17.title: Pangandaran earthquake and tsunami
07-17.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Java on July 17, 2006, generated a tsunami that struck about 300 kilometres of southern coastline, including Pangandaran. A field-survey study reports 668 deaths, 65 people missing and 9,299 receiving medical treatment.

07-17.title: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 Shootdown
07-17.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 was shot down over eastern Ukraine on July 17, 2014, killing all 298 passengers and crew. Dutch investigations concluded that a Buk surface-to-air missile was fired from separatist-controlled territory. A Dutch court convicted three men for their roles in the downing.
sources: District Court of The Hague, judgment transcript

07-20.title: Horn of Africa famine in Somalia
07-20.description: The UN declared famine in parts of southern Somalia on July 20, 2011. A FAO/FSNAU and FEWS NET study published in 2013 estimated approximately 258,000 excess deaths from severe food insecurity between October 2010 and April 2012, including about 133,000 children under five. Estimated mortality peaked at about 30,000 excess deaths per month from May through August 2011.

07-20.title: Aurora theater shooting
07-20.description: A gunman attacked a midnight screening of The Dark Knight Rises at a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado, on July 20, 2012, killing 12 people and injuring 70. James Holmes was convicted and in 2015 received 12 consecutive life sentences without parole, plus additional prison terms.

07-21.title: Beijing floods
07-21.description: Exceptional rain on July 21-22, 2012, caused severe flooding in Beijing. It was the city's heaviest rainfall in 61 years. Later assessments reported 79 deaths, at least 8,200 homes destroyed and approximately 11.6 billion yuan in losses.

07-22.title: Norway terror attacks (Oslo bombing and Utoya massacre)
07-22.description: On July 22, 2011, Anders Behring Breivik killed eight people in a bombing in Oslo and 69 in a shooting attack on a youth camp on Utoya, for 77 victims in total. He was convicted and sentenced to preventive detention initially set at 21 years, extendable if he remained dangerous.

07-22.title: Munich Olympia shopping mall shooting
07-22.description: A gunman killed nine people at and near Munich's Olympia shopping centre on July 22, 2016, before killing himself. The city officially commemorates the attack as racist and right-wing terrorism. The toll excludes the attacker.

07-23.title: Kabul twin bombing of Hazara demonstration
07-23.description: Two suicide bombers attacked a peaceful demonstration at Kabul's Deh Mazang square on July 23, 2016. UNAMA documented 85 civilian deaths and 413 injuries. Islamic State's local affiliate claimed responsibility.
sources: UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan, 2016 annual civilian protection report

07-24.title: Angara Airlines Flight 2311 crash
07-24.description: On July 24, 2025, an Angara Airlines Antonov An-24 operating Flight 2311 crashed near Tynda in Russia's Amur region while approaching its destination. All 42 passengers and six crew members died.

07-26.title: Ahmedabad serial bombings
07-26.description: A series of bombings in Ahmedabad on July 26, 2008 killed 56 people and injured more than 200. The targets included hospitals. In February 2022, a special court sentenced 38 defendants to death and 11 to life imprisonment in the bombing case.
sources: The Indian Express: Ahmedabad bombing sentences, February 18, 2022
Ministry of Home Affairs: tribunal order published August 6, 2024

07-26.title: Gansu flash flood at Weiyuan scenic area
07-26.description: A flash flood struck a scenic area in Weiyuan County, Dingxi City, on the afternoon of 26 July 2026, killing 25 people and injuring 23. China's national disaster commission said it would oversee an investigation into the disaster and urged Gansu Province to strengthen disaster prevention, mitigation and relief capacity.

07-27.title: Sknyliv air show disaster
07-27.description: A Ukrainian Air Force Su-27 crashed into spectators during an aerobatic display at Sknyliv airfield near Lviv on 27 July 2002. The disaster killed 77 people, including 28 children, and injured hundreds.

07-28.title: Kumamoto earthquake
07-28.description: An earthquake measured at magnitude 7.1 by Japan's Meteorological Agency struck Kumamoto at 16:27 local time on 28 July 2026. Prefectural figures as of 3 August recorded 38 deaths, 98 injuries and 8,383 evacuees. Damage included an explosion and collapse at Aeon Mall in Kashima and a chimney collapse at a paper mill in Yatsushiro.

07-29.title: Wayanad Landslides
07-29.description: Landslides struck Wayanad, Kerala, early on July 30, 2024 local time, July 29 UTC, after intense rain. A government answer to Parliament in April 2025 reported 298 deaths, including 32 missing people declared deceased, based on Kerala's official accounting.

07-29.title: Firefighting helicopter crash in San Juan kills seven
07-29.description: A Bell 412 helicopter contracted by Argentina's Federal Emergency Agency crashed near Ischigualasto Provincial Park in San Juan on 29 July 2026, killing all seven occupants. It had previously taken part in training and was travelling toward La Rioja to assist firefighting operations. Contact was lost at about 10:26 local time.

07-29.title: Wildfires in southern Greece kill three firefighters
07-29.location: Rethymno, Crete and Gytheio, Laconia, Greece
07-29.description: Three firefighters died during wildfire response operations in southern Greece on 29 July 2026. Two died in a fire in the Rethymno region of Crete. A third was found unconscious near a fire in the Gytheio area and pronounced dead in hospital; authorities had not established the cause of his death.

07-30.title: Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh
07-30.description: Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh and his bodyguard were killed at a residence in Tehran around 2 a.m. on July 31, 2024 local time, July 30 UTC. Accounts differed over whether a projectile or a previously planted explosive caused the blast.

07-30.title: Broad Peak avalanche kills ten climbers
07-30.description: An avalanche struck ten climbers on Broad Peak in Pakistan's Karakoram range on the morning of 30 July 2026. All ten, including Nirmal Purja, were subsequently confirmed dead. Recovery operations continued after the first bodies were located, with weather and terrain hindering access.

07-31.title: Kaohsiung Gas Explosions
07-31.description: A series of underground gas explosions ripped through streets in Kaohsiung, killing 32 people and injuring over 300. The blasts were caused by leaking propylene gas in sewer systems.
sources: Taiwan Ministry of Environment, incident review

07-31.title: Flash floods and landslides in Dien Bien Province
07-31.description: Flash floods and landslides struck Dien Bien Province early on 1 August 2025 local time (31 July UTC), after heavy rain. A subsequent provincial tally reported ten deaths and seven injuries. Homes and roads were damaged and several communities isolated.

07-31.title: Terrorist attack on labourers in Kulgam
07-31.description: Gunmen shot two workers from Chhattisgarh at a brick kiln in Kelam, Kulgam district, on the evening of 31 July 2026. One died initially and the second later died in hospital, bringing the death toll to two.

08-01.title: Bombing at Moscow restaurant kills five
08-01.description: A bomb exploded near the Balzi Rossi restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in Moscow on the evening of 1 August 2026. Authorities initially reported three deaths, including the woman carrying the device, a security guard and a visitor. A subsequent Russian embassy statement reported five dead and 19 injured.

08-01.title: Israeli strikes kill at least seven in Gaza
08-01.description: Gaza's civil defence reported seven people killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip since dawn on 1 August 2026. An Israeli strike also destroyed medical supplies stored for Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, according to hospital and Palestinian health officials.

08-01.title: Taliban police report killing seven alleged robbers in Kabul
08-01.description: Taliban police said seven men accused of armed robbery were killed during an operation in Kabul's Police District 8 on 1 August 2026. Police described a confrontation at about 21:00 local time. A former Afghan justice minister subsequently described the killings as extrajudicial; the police account was not independently established.

08-02.title: Drone strike on Darfur community court kills at least 46, rights group reports
08-02.description: A drone strike hit Zawiya Ghara community court in North Darfur during a court session on 2 August 2026. Emergency Lawyers initially reported at least 35 deaths. Darfur Victims Support Organization later reported 46 civilian deaths and seven injuries in preliminary documentation based on interviews with families and witnesses. Rights groups attributed the strike to the Sudanese army.

08-02.title: Firefighting helicopters collide in Greece killing two
08-02.description: Two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air on Sunday while battling a wind-driven wildfire west of Athens, and one caught fire and crashed. A Greek and a Danish crew member died; the two survivors — a Greek and a British national — were taken to hospital in Athens.

08-02.title: Israeli strikes kill 18 in Gaza
08-02.description: Israeli airstrikes across Gaza on 2 August 2026 killed at least 18 Palestinians, including children, according to medics. Strikes hit Gaza City, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis. The toll may overlap the 18 newly killed people in the health ministry's next-day 24-hour bulletin and must not be counted again.

08-02.title: Russian glide bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia
08-02.description: Russian aircraft dropped eight glide bombs on residential districts of Zaporizhzhia within 90 minutes on Sunday evening, killing a 71-year-old woman, wounding 31 people — including a 16-year-old girl — and damaging 22 apartment buildings in four districts of the city.

08-03.title: El Paso Walmart shooting
08-03.description: A gunman targeting Hispanic shoppers attacked the Cielo Vista Walmart in El Paso, Texas, on August 3, 2019. Twenty-three people died and 22 were injured. The attacker pleaded guilty to federal hate-crime and firearms charges and was sentenced in July 2023 to 90 consecutive life terms.

08-03.title: Drone crash on Gelendzhik-area beach kills eight
08-03.description: A drone crashed onto a beach at Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik on the morning of 3 August 2026. Later reporting put the toll at eight deaths, including four children, with 58 injured. Russia attributed the drone to Ukraine; whether air defences caused it to crash remained uncertain.

08-03.title: Israeli strike kills two in Gaza City
08-03.description: An Israeli airstrike targeted a vehicle southwest of Gaza City on Monday evening, killing two Palestinians in the Sheikh Ajlin area, in another violation of the ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, medical sources said.

08-03.title: Russian guided bombs kill three in Sumy
08-03.description: Russian guided aerial bombs struck Sumy between 02:08 and 02:17 local time on 4 August 2026 (3 August UTC). The attack killed two girls aged five and ten and a 75-year-old woman, according to Ukrainian reports, and injured other residents. Homes and civilian infrastructure were damaged.

08-04.title: Beirut Port Explosion
08-04.description: An ammonium nitrate explosion at the Port of Beirut on August 4, 2020 killed 218 people and wounded about 7,000, according to Human Rights Watch's investigation.

08-04.title: Lightning strike kills footballer in Thailand
08-04.description: A lightning strike during a Golok FA Cup match at Santiphap Stadium in Sungai Golok, Narathiwat, on the afternoon of 4 August 2026 killed 24-year-old Yala FC player Sofwan Awae. At least nine others were reported injured.

08-05.title: Wisconsin Sikh temple shooting
08-05.description: A white supremacist gunman attacked the Sikh Temple of Wisconsin in Oak Creek on August 5, 2012. Six victims died that day, and Baba Punjab Singh died from complications of his injuries in 2020, bringing the victim toll to seven. The attacker also died by suicide; he is not included in the victim count.

08-05.title: Explosion in southern Lebanon kills two Israeli soldiers
08-05.description: Two Israeli reservists from Battalion 2855 of the 55th Reserve Paratroopers Brigade were killed and four seriously wounded in an explosion during an operation in Majdal Zoun on 5 August 2026, the Israeli military announced the following day. The circumstances of the explosive device were under investigation.

08-05.title: Israeli airstrike on south Lebanon kills one
08-05.description: An Israeli drone strike hit the roof of a prayer hall at a cemetery in Tebnine, Bint Jbeil district, on 5 August 2026. Lebanon's Health Ministry reported one person killed and twelve injured, updating an initial report of eleven injuries. The strike came as a round of Lebanese-Israeli talks in Rome concluded.

08-05.title: Mass shooting in Caswell County, North Carolina kills three
08-05.location: Caswell County, North Carolina, United States
08-05.description: A mass shooting at a rural home in Caswell County, North Carolina, left three family members dead - including the suspected shooter - and a fourth relative hospitalized, according to the Caswell County Sheriff's Office and the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation.

08-05.title: Rain-triggered house collapse kills six in Pratapgarh, India
08-05.description: A house collapsed during heavy rain in Mahuli, Pratapgarh district, at about 2 a.m. local time on August 6, killing six members of a family, including two young children.

08-06.title: ATF operation in Nashville ends with man and teenager fatally shot
08-06.description: James Salinas, 32, and Denzel Molina, 16, were fatally shot during an ATF firearms operation on Landers Avenue in Nashville on August 6. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said agents encountered two people and gunfire was exchanged; it was investigating the circumstances. No officers were injured.

08-06.title: Russian drone strike on Lozova train station kills two
08-06.description: Russian drones struck railway infrastructure and the station in Lozova on August 6, killing two railway workers aged 52 and 59 and injuring 11 people, according to regional police.

08-06.title: Wildfire kills bulldozer operator in Oregon
08-06.description: Jason Ensign, a 47-year-old equipment operator, died while operating a bulldozer at the Wrights Spring Fire in Oregon on August 6. Rapid fire growth cut off his escape route while he helped construct fire lines.

08-07.title: Russo-Georgian War
08-07.description: Heavy fighting began around Tskhinvali in South Ossetia on the night of August 7-8, 2008 and expanded into a five-day war involving Georgian and Russian forces and separatist forces. The EU fact-finding mission estimated about 850 deaths across the conflict from the parties' reported losses and said far more than 100,000 civilians fled their homes.
sources: EU Independent International Fact-Finding Mission: volume I
Human Rights Watch: Up in Flames, January 2009
Human Rights Watch: cluster-munition investigation, April 2009

08-07.title: Firefighting helicopter crash near Utah wildfire kills two
08-07.description: Two pilots died when a contracted CH-54A firefighting helicopter crashed near Kanosh at about 10:41 a.m. local time on August 7 while dropping water on the Widemouth 2 Fire.

08-07.title: Thailand school shooting kills nine
08-07.description: A student killed his grandparents before attacking Debsirin Nonthaburi School on the morning of August 7, killing five staff members and injuring more than 20 people. The shooter also died. A wounded pupil died on August 8, bringing the reported total, including the shooter and the grandparents, to nine.

08-08.title: Maui wildfire
08-08.description: A wildfire that began near Lahaina, Maui, on the morning of August 8, 2023 local time later spread through the town. Investigators found that broken electrical lines started the fire and surviving embers rekindled in strong winds. The confirmed toll reached 102 after a later death was attributed to fire injuries in June 2024.

08-08.title: Helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro kills four
08-08.location: Alto da Boa Vista, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
08-08.description: A Robinson 44 helicopter crashed in a forested area near Vista Chinesa in the Tijuca National Park in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday morning, killing all four people on board, firefighters said.

08-09.title: Sbarro Pizzeria Bombing
08-09.description: A suicide bombing at the Sbarro pizzeria in Jerusalem on 9 August 2001 killed 15 civilians initially and wounded about 130. Chana Nachenberg died in May 2023 after remaining unconscious since the attack, bringing the victim toll to 16, excluding the bomber.

08-09.title: Saada school bus airstrike
08-09.description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a school bus at Dahyan market in Saada Governorate on August 9, 2018. The ICRC relayed a local-authority tally of 51 dead, including 40 children, and 79 injured.

08-09.title: Voepass Flight 2283 Crash
08-09.description: Voepass Flight 2283, an ATR 72-500 flying from Cascavel to Sao Paulo-Guarulhos, crashed in Vinhedo on August 9, 2024. All 58 passengers and four crew members died. The crash occurred well into the flight, not shortly after takeoff.

08-09.title: Landslide on rain-soaked hillside in Baguio kills 10
08-09.description: A landslide struck houses in Guisad Surong, Baguio, on the evening of August 9 during prolonged monsoon rain. By early August 11, rescuers had accounted for all 13 reported victims: ten died and three survived.

08-09.title: Russian missile strike on Kharkiv apartment block kills two
08-09.description: Russian missiles struck a high-rise apartment block in Kharkiv's Saltivskyi district on Sunday morning, August 9, killing two people, two men aged 50 and 66, and injuring more than a dozen others, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov.

08-09.title: Sofa factory fire in Riyadh kills 16 Bangladeshi workers
08-09.description: A fire broke out on Sunday at a sofa manufacturing factory in the Musa Sanaiya industrial area of Riyadh, killing at least 16 Bangladeshi migrant workers, according to Bangladesh's Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry. Ten of the victims were from the Naogaon district and others from Natore and Rajshahi.

08-09.title: Two tribal elders shot dead in South Waziristan, Pakistan
08-09.location: Toi Khulla, Lower South Waziristan, Pakistan
08-09.description: Unidentified gunmen killed tribal elders Haji Gul and Malik Badshah while they traveled toward Zarmilan in Lower South Waziristan on August 9. Police said the attack occurred near Darozanda in Toi Khulla tehsil; both men belonged to the Suleman Khel tribe.

08-10.title: Typhoon Saomai strikes China
08-10.description: Typhoon Saomai made landfall in Zhejiang on August 10, 2006. The Hong Kong Observatory's annual account records at least 460 deaths across Zhejiang, Fujian and Jiangxi, about two million people evacuated and 60,000 houses destroyed.

08-10.title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake in western Colombia kills at least 331
08-10.location: Western Colombia (Choco; Cali, Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo)
08-10.description: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia at 12:34 UTC on August 10, with its epicenter near San Jose del Palmar, Choco. UNGRD's September 3 assessment reported 331 deaths and 466,606 people affected. Buildings collapsed and landslides damaged communities in the affected region.

08-10.title: Murder-suicide at Chicago elementary school leaves two custodians dead
08-10.description: A shooting at Mark Twain Elementary School in Chicago's Garfield Ridge neighborhood on August 10 killed custodian Amalia Bautista Perez, 48, and her 63-year-old coworker. The medical examiner classified their deaths as homicide and suicide respectively. No children were in the school.

08-10.title: Palestinian girl dies of wounds from Israeli fire in Gaza
08-10.location: Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, Gaza Strip, Palestine
08-10.description: Thirteen-year-old Saba Naim Abdullah al-Hashash died on August 10 from wounds sustained when Israeli forces shot her several days earlier in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, according to WAFA.

08-10.title: Russian artillery strike on Buhaivka village in Kharkiv region kills five
08-10.location: Buhaivka, Chuhuiv district, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine
08-10.description: Russian forces carried out a massive artillery strike on the residential area of the village of Buhaivka in the Chuhuiv district of Kharkiv Oblast on August 10, killing five people and destroying several houses, according to regional authorities and the prosecutor's office.

08-10.title: Russian strike on Zaporizhstal kills eight workers
08-10.description: A Russian ballistic-missile attack struck the Zaporizhstal steel plant around 00:30 local time on August 11, or August 10 UTC. The plant later reported eight employees killed and 26 injured in that attack, which halted production.

08-11.title: Ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba killing 46
08-11.description: An overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba on August 11 after encountering strong waves. Police reported 46 deaths by August 13, while the disaster-management agency said 77 people had been rescued. Authorities had not established a definitive passenger or missing-person count.

08-11.title: Ferry fire off Bali kills one
08-11.description: The Putri Yasmin ferry caught fire between Bali and Lombok around 4:15 a.m. local time on August 12, or August 11 UTC. Rescuers evacuated 211 people and recovered a 19-year-old Indonesian woman's body, authorities reported.

08-11.title: Landslide on Mumbai chawl kills eight
08-11.description: A rain-triggered landslide struck homes at Gaushiya Chawl in Chirag Nagar, Mumbai, around 3:48 a.m. local time on August 12, or August 11 UTC. The death toll rose to eight before search operations ended on August 13; seven others were injured.

08-11.title: Russian strike on tanker truck in Odesa region kills two
08-11.description: A Russian strike hit a tanker truck containing oil residue in Odesa region on August 11. Regional administration head Oleh Kiper reported two people killed and three wounded.

08-12.title: Military Apache helicopter crash near Salado kills two
08-12.description: An AH-64 Apache attack helicopter from Fort Hood crashed into a field south of Salado, Texas, around 1:35 p.m. local time, killing both pilots on board and igniting a grass fire that forced nearby residents to flee.

08-13.title: Armed man fatally shot by police at Auckland shopping centre
08-13.description: An armed man fleeing from police was shot and killed at Sylvia Park Shopping Centre in Auckland on Thursday afternoon. Police said the man had stolen an air rifle from a gun shop in Penrose; he was confronted under an overpass and pronounced dead at the scene despite first aid.

08-13.title: Bomb blast kills defected naval officer in Sevastopol
08-13.description: An explosion in Sevastopol on the morning of August 13 killed a Russian naval officer later identified in reporting as Robert Shageyev, a former Ukrainian submarine commander who defected in 2014. Russian authorities said they detained a woman and alleged Ukrainian intelligence involvement; that allegation was not independently verified.

08-13.title: Explosion at Fujian shipyard kills firefighter
08-13.description: A fire at Huahai Shipyard in Gantang, Fu'an, began at 13:09 local time on August 13. An explosion at 14:10 injured ten firefighters and two other people; one firefighter died in hospital that evening. Authorities were investigating the cause.

08-13.title: Explosion at Port of Rotterdam kills one
08-13.description: An explosion at the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands killed at least one person and injured several others on August 13, 2026. Dutch regional broadcaster Rijnmond reported the blast occurred at around 11:30 a.m. local time; Rotterdam police said the cause remained under investigation and emergency services scaled up their response.

08-13.title: Firecracker factory explosion near Sivakasi kills two workers
08-13.description: Two men died after an explosion while testing a new chemical-mixing machine at a fireworks factory near Sivakasi on August 13. One died at the site and the second in hospital. Police opened an investigation into the cause.

08-13.title: Israeli strikes kill two Palestinians in Gaza
08-13.description: Israeli strikes killed Gaza police official Jamal Abu Kamil in Gaza City and Hudhaifa Kawara in Khan Younis on August 13, according to Palestinian medical and interior-ministry sources. Israel said Abu Kamil was a Hamas commander.

08-13.title: Landslide and water seepage in Chamoli tunnel kills seven workers
08-13.description: A sudden influx of water and debris entered the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti project's unfinished tunnel in Chamoli around 6:20 p.m. local time on August 13. At least seven workers died and others were injured, with searches continuing for missing workers.

08-13.title: Mudslide in Changxing, Zhejiang kills one and leaves three missing
08-13.description: A rain-triggered mudslide collapsed a house in Tanlongqiao village, Heping town, Changxing, around 6:30 a.m. local time on August 14, or August 13 UTC. County authorities reported one confirmed death and three people missing that afternoon.

08-13.title: Multi-vehicle crash near Accra kills at least 11
08-13.description: A multi-vehicle collision on the Accra-Kumasi highway at Ofankor Barrier in Ghana's capital killed at least 11 people and injured 13 others in the early hours of August 13, 2026, according to the Ghana National Fire Service. The service said it received a distress call at about 4:00 a.m. local time regarding the collision.

08-13.title: Record rainfall in Chiba kills thirteen
08-13.description: Record rainfall on August 13-14 flooded communities in Chiba Prefecture. The governor reported thirteen deaths, one person missing and damage to more than 4,500 homes by August 27.

08-13.title: Russian drone strike on passenger train in Odesa region kills two
08-13.description: A Russian drone struck a passenger train in Berezivka district, Odesa region, on August 13, killing the driver and his assistant. Authorities evacuated the 340 passengers, including 67 children; no passengers were reported injured.

08-13.title: Suspected murder-suicide shooting on Staten Island kills two
08-13.location: Staten Island, New York, United States
